clue.text: Pull dependant back

indicators.note: 'back' as in going back the way you came: the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a ward is a dependant in a guardian's care; read it back to front

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a person who relies on them back to safety.
explanation.walkthrough: A ward is a child or dependant legally under a guardian's care, a common crossword source for these four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: horses draw a carriage, and a smoker draws on a pipe, both meaning pull.

clue.text: Tarnished tin made a shiny material

indicators.note: a tarnished thing has been spoiled from its original state, so the letters are no longer in their original order

explanation.surface: A dull metal is somehow turned into something glittering.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts tarnished and shiny, as if describing polishing; 'made a' belongs to the fodder rather than being a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the word is French for 'set with diamonds', and it names fabric or trim covered in glittering glass or sequins.

clue.text: Remove top of beam later

indicators.note: in a down answer the word stands upright, so its top is its first letter, and that is what comes off

parts.note: a rafter is a roof beam; take off its first letter R

explanation.surface: An instruction to a builder to take the upper part off a beam at a later stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Later' looks like a time for the building job; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adverbs: 'we'll talk about it after' and 'we'll talk about it later' say the same.

clue.text: Scholar's account interrupted by media broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered too
a speech interrupted by heckling has the heckling break into its middle, so the second part sits inside the first

parts.note: ACC is a standard abbreviation for account; it splits AC…C
MEDIA rearranged, placed between AC and C

explanation.surface: A scholar's version of events is cut short by a news broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: '’s' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a university lecturer or researcher is called an academic, a scholar by profession.

clue.text: Cook at once sees hot snack

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so the letters are doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to get cooking straight away once someone spots a hot snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot snack' reads as one phrase, but HOT is needed in the fodder, so the definition is just 'snack'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: grated cheese melted under the grill on a slice of toast is a classic British light bite.

clue.text: Five hundred pixies shortened burrow

indicators.note: a word that is shortened has been cut down, and here it loses its final letter

parts.note: pixies are elves; ELVES without its last letter

explanation.surface: Five hundred small magical creatures, cut back in number, digging underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the pixies are doing the burrowing; 'burrow' is the verb that defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to delve was originally to dig with a spade, and to burrow is to dig into the ground.

clue.text: Main rock almost formed island

indicators.note: almost the whole word means stopping one letter short of its end
clay that is formed is shaped into something new, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A piece of geology: rock rising from the sea to make an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'the main', the open sea, which suits an island story; here it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Minorca (Menorca) is one of the Balearic islands off Spain.

clue.text: Animal scoffing hot dog

indicators.note: to scoff food is to gobble it up, so the first word swallows the letter that follows

parts.note: a cow is an animal; it opens to take in the next letter
H = hot, as on a tap; goes inside COW

explanation.surface: A creature wolfing down a hot dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' reads as the sausage in a bun; it splits into H and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the chow chow is a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy in shape

definitions.meaning: slang for an old-fashioned, conventional person
a four-sided figure with equal sides

explanation.surface: An old fogey who is keeping fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In shape' reads as fit; the two words part and 'shape' becomes the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: 1950s slang for someone stuffy and out of touch, and the geometric figure with four equal sides.

clue.text: Old and short, quite wrinkled

indicators.note: a word that is short of something is missing a bit, here its last letter
a wrinkled sheet has been creased out of its smooth order, so the letters are rumpled

explanation.surface: Describing an elderly person: aged, small and rather wrinkly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of height, alongside 'old' and 'wrinkled'; it tells you to trim 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym: antique furniture is old furniture, though the word usually implies value too.

clue.text: Jargon in advance written on back of manual

indicators.note: text written on something is added on after it, so these letters follow
the back of a word is its end, so take its last letter

explanation.surface: Technical terms printed on the back cover of an instruction manual, ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In advance' reads as 'beforehand'; the two words split, and 'in' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: lingo is informal for the special vocabulary of a trade or group, which is what jargon is.

clue.text: Vessel in amphora, or tankard

indicators.note: the answer is literally in the words that follow, running across the gaps between them

explanation.surface: Where to find a drinking vessel: an ancient jar or a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a pot, like the amphora and tankard that follow; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the body's main artery is the largest of the blood vessels.

clue.text: Fluff found in modest drink

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so the first word goes into the second

parts.note: shy = modest, retiring; it opens around the other part
to fluff a line is to make a mistake, to err; goes inside SHY

explanation.surface: Some lint discovered in an unassuming glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' reads as lint; it is the verb to bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a fortified wine from around Jerez in Spain is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Mushroom, advocaat and lemonade

definitions.meaning: the verb: to grow very rapidly
a cocktail mixing Dutch egg liqueur with fizzy lemonade

explanation.surface: A list of odd ingredients: a fungus with egg liqueur and a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' looks like a noun among the ingredients; it is the verb to grow fast. Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur, and the cocktail is a British Christmas favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a problem that mushrooms grows like a ball rolled through snow, and the pub cocktail of advocaat topped with lemonade.

clue.text: Ultimate ban on rocky peak that's flat

indicators.note: something rocky is unsteady and wobbles about, so the letters shift out of place

explanation.surface: A final ban on climbing a craggy summit that turns out to be level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimate ban' tempts you to take the last letter of 'ban'; all three words are fodder, and 'rocky' belongs to the peak in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the mountain above Cape Town is famous for its level top, like a tabletop.

clue.text: State showing little interest in colour during time of prosperity

indicators.note: something that happens during a period falls within it, so the colour sits inside the boom

parts.note: a boom is a period of prosperity; it opens around the colour
red is a colour; goes inside BOOM

explanation.surface: A mood of indifference to colour in good economic times.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive phrase, easy to mistake for part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the condition of feeling weary and uninterested is the noun for being bored.

clue.text: One, perhaps, is less sensitive

definitions.meaning: one is an example, so 'perhaps' flags a definition by example
more lacking in feeling: a comparative adjective, not a noun

explanation.surface: A remark that a single person may feel less.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is two words spelt alike: the noun (NUM-ber) and the comparative of numb (NUMM-er).
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one is a numeral, and something numb-er has lost more of its feeling.

clue.text: For example, some chicken run circled by wild animal

indicators.note: a thing circled by another is ringed round by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a beast is a wild animal; it opens around the R
R = run, as in cricket scores; goes inside BEAST

explanation.surface: A chicken coop surrounded by a predator such as a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken run' reads as the hen enclosure; it splits into the definition and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: white meat from the front of the bird is one cut of chicken you might buy.

clue.text: Protective garment worn regularly after month in spring

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter

parts.note: APR is the calendar abbreviation for April

indicators.note: coming after the month, so these letters follow it

parts.note: second and fourth letters of wORN

explanation.surface: A garment put on often once April comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' reads as describing the garment; it is the source of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a cloth tied over the front of the body to keep clothes clean is a protective garment.

clue.text: Bird beginning to make a raucous cry

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a caw is a harsh cry, like a crow's

explanation.surface: A bird starting to squawk loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes the bird itself, and 'beginning to make' reads as 'starting to make' rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the large, loud, brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America is a bird.

clue.text: Strike beginning to affect country

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An industrial strike starting to hit a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' reads as a walkout; it is the informal verb to chin, to hit on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the People's Republic in East Asia is a country.

clue.text: Learning, no end, for macho man

indicators.note: with no end, the word has lost its final letter

parts.note: study = learning; drop its last letter Y

explanation.surface: Endless education for a tough guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' could mean 'a great deal'; here it trims one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a stud is a stallion kept for breeding, and by extension a virile, macho man.

clue.text: Strange tour taking in back of terraced house

indicators.note: strange means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their ordinary order
the back of a word is its end, so take its last letter

parts.note: TOUR rearranged, split around the next letter

indicators.note: a house taking in a lodger holds them inside, so the letter goes inside

explanation.surface: An odd guided walk that goes round the back of a row house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terraced house' reads as one thing, a house in a row; 'house' alone is the definition, meaning a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a dynasty, and the Tudors ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Country song featured in musical

definitions.meaning: the usual short name for the United States
a number sung by the Sharks girls in West Side Story

explanation.surface: A country-and-western number in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' reads as country music; 'Country' stands alone as the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the United States, and the Bernstein–Sondheim number from West Side Story.

clue.text: Revolutionary made it with no control

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel who succeeded without any leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the subject, a rebel; it is the anagram signal, and 'no control' reads as a phrase though 'control' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to hold sway over something, to have the upper hand over it, is to control it.

clue.text: Everything going past bat originally — for example, a bouncer

indicators.note: a thing going past another ends up beyond it, so these letters come after
originally means at the start, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: Everything flying past a cricket bat, like a short-pitched delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' reads as a nightclub doorman; in cricket it is a short delivery that rears up at the batter's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a bouncer is one kind of cricket delivery, and any bouncing sphere is also one.
